{"id":"mimid-604m.2","title":"A first private message is I/O-sensitive by 30x: find its write and fsync count","description":"`private_queries_are_one_to_one_rooms` (crates/mimid-agent/tests/irc_v2.rs)
ran 349.61s, 375.65s and 11.77s on the same code. The two slow runs
followed a `cargo clean`: cold page cache, a full rebuild competing for
the disk, and 178 GiB freed on the filesystem underneath. The fast run
was a warm build with nothing competing. So the path is not slow; it is
I/O-sensitive by three orders of magnitude, which is the same thing to
a user on a loaded phone.

## What to find

What a first private message does between the `PRIVMSG` and the line
coming back. The pieces, from the crate map: `Store::action` creates the
one-to-one room, the agent fetches a KeyPackage, creates the MLS group,
sends a Welcome, and `Store::sync` reads the journal back. Each of those
touches `mimid.sqlite` and OpenMLS's state in the same database.

The question to answer with numbers, not reading: how many write
transactions and how many fsyncs does one private query cost? A path
that commits per MLS operation rather than per user action multiplies
every disk stall by that count, and that multiplier is what turns 11s
into 350s.

## Method

Depends on bead mimid-604m.1 (the daemon logs nothing). With a
subscriber installed, a span per step and `sqlx`'s slow-statement
warning already at 1s, one slow run names the step. Reproduce the
pressure deliberately rather than waiting for another `cargo clean`:
run the test while a second process writes to the same filesystem.

## Not a fix for the test

The test is correct and its wait has no deadline any more, so it
measures rather than fails. Do not make it wait differently.

That is what both slow runs (349.61s, 375.65s) and the 2.4s PRAGMA were measured under, and it is still running: mimid-agent-core's own lib unit tests (frank::tests, agent::didwebvh_tests, which no sweep touched) each take over 60 seconds right now against seconds when the machine is idle. So the 30x figure in this bead's title is a measurement under a 4.5x CPU oversubscription, not a property of the first-DM path alone. Re-measure deliberately: run the test alone, then again under a known load, rather than waiting to be surprised. The bug in mimid-604m still stands -- the agent says nothing while it waits -- and bead mimid-604m.1 is what makes the next measurement readable."}
